SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaints: 
  • Decreased hearing in left ear for ~6 weeks, intermittent.  
  • Intermittent ringing (tinnitus) in left ear, sometimes triggered by TV/music.  
  • Occasional mild dizziness/off-balance sensation; no true vertigo or associated nausea.  
  • No ear pain, no otorrhea, no fever, no chest pain, no palpitations.
- Past medical history: not discussed.
- Medications: not documented.
- Social history: not elicited.
- Allergies: not documented.

Objective:
- No in-clinic examination performed (video consult only).
- No vitals available.
- Investigations to date: none.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left-sided hearing loss  
   - Assessment: Suspected conductive loss (rule out impacted cerumen or other external/middle-ear pathology).  
   - Differential diagnosis: impacted cerumen; otitis media with effusion; eustachian tube dysfunction; sensorineural loss.  
   - Investigations planned: Face-to-face appointment within 4–5 days for otoscopic examination and hearing assessment.  
   - Treatment planned: Will depend on findings (e.g., cerumen removal if wax impaction identified).  

2. Tinnitus (left ear)  
   - Assessment: Tinnitus of uncertain etiology.  
   - Investigations planned: As above; further audiology/ENT referral if persistent after ear exam.  
   - Treatment/management: Provided patient education—link to tinnitus information leaflet placed in chart.  

3. Episodic dizziness  
   - Assessment: Mild disequilibrium, likely secondary to ear pathology.  
   - Investigations planned: Otoscopic exam; consider vestibular assessment if symptoms persist after ear clearance.  

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: allergies, current medication list, social history.  
• Internal conflicts: none noted.  
• Transcript quality: clear; minor background conversation but clinically adequate.
